text: The book links reservoir CPGs to motor neuroscience. Which pairing correctly matches an empirical finding with its reservoir-computing model?
choices: Place cells (O'Keefe) paired with a ridge-regression readout of the Lorenz attractor

Churchland et al. (2012) rotational population dynamics in motor cortex paired with the Sussillo & Abbott (2009) FORCE-trained recurrent network that reproduces those rotations with only its readout trained
Cerebellar climbing fibers paired with the fixed random input weights W_in of an ESN
Working-memory persistent activity paired with a reservoir whose spectral radius is far below 1
explanation: Churchland et al. (2012) found rotational dynamics in motor-cortex population activity; Sussillo & Abbott (2009) showed a FORCE-trained RNN (recurrent weights fixed, only the readout learned) reproduces such rotations, which is the reservoir link. Option 2 is wrong (climbing fibers are the error/teacher signal, not W_in); option 3 is wrong (persistent working memory needs rho ~ 1, near marginal stability, not far below 1); option 0 pairs unrelated items.
